new.s: Under the Charter Act of 1853, what replaced the patronage of the Directors in civil service appointments?
o: Nomination by the Board of Control
new.x: The Charter Act of 1853 ended the Directors' patronage and threw the civil services open to competitive examination.

new.x: The Directors appointed civil servants till 1853, when the Charter Act of 1853 introduced open competition.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Charter Act of 1853:
1. It separated the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's Council.
2. It renewed the Company's charter for 20 years.

new.x: The 1853 Act separated legislative from executive work, but renewed the Company's rule with no fixed term, not 20 years.
new.angle: U0175 #1 Charter Act 1853 -> separate legislature, no fixed term

new.s: Which land revenue system was introduced in the North-Western Provinces (Agra-Oudh)?
new.x: The Mahalwari system, proposed by Holt Mackenzie in 1822, covered the North-Western Provinces, parts of Punjab and Central India.

new.s: Which of the following areas did NOT come under the Mahalwari system?
new.x: Madras was under the Ryotwari system; the Mahalwari system covered the North-Western Provinces, parts of Punjab, the Gangetic valley and Central India.

new.s: To which of Cornwallis's measures was the rise in litigation after 1793 mainly traced?
new.x: More lawsuits after 1793 were traced to Cornwallis's judicial reforms, especially the abolition of court fees.
